interview.q1: Uma redação nova, em inglês, sobre a Web Summit, que tem uma página sobre nós. On the phone it looked like a news site with an agenda; by the end it looked like a RiskMandate project that asks every company the same three security questions, with a nice news site around it.
interview.q2: Dinis Cruz and two other editors, one of them only 'Vicky', with AI agents doing the actual work, and the same team works on RiskMandate. Also something called web-summit.sgit.ai. I could not tell which company is legally behind it.
interview.q3: Partly. The facts about us are correct and every one has a source and a date, and they say openly that they are not independent of RiskMandate, which most sponsored media never admit. But the pound meter, the 'team's notes on whether to meet', and About saying changes go live without human review make me careful about giving them my words.
interview.q4: Nothing urgent: the page is right, so there is nothing to correct. I forward it to my cofounder today. If anything, after the summit, I might answer the three questions in writing, once I know who reads them and that a person checks the text before it goes up.
interview.q5: Maybe, leaning no for now. The page is correct, so the 'is your page right?' hook gives me no reason to reply, and the 15 minute ask during the summit week, from a two-day-old site tied to a security vendor, loses to everything else in my calendar.
interview.q6: One line at the top of our page, in Portuguese, from Dinis: 'RiskMandate does not pay for or see your answer; you approve your words before they are published', and a plain 'reply / correct this page' button. Then I would answer in two lines.

findings.finding: The '£4.99' button sits unlabelled in the phone nav next to 'Vault', so a founder arriving from an outreach email reads it as a paywall or a pay-to-be-featured price.
The reading meter 'This page 0.5p of 5p', 'Balance £4.99' and 'Rate it, or do not pay for it' is never explained on the page and reinforces the suspicion of paid media.

The email promises the page shows 'onde está no mapa da IA da cimeira', but the page files the company only under 'Portuguese startups', and front-phone-s6 shows an 'AI agents' field (22) it is not in.
'We have not asked ChatPlace yet. When they answer, it goes here.' contradicts the email that is asking them, so the page looks stale the moment the recipient lands.
Mentioning that the team's notes record 'whether to meet' and 'who owns it' for each company tells the founder she is a lead in a pipeline, without saying whose.
About says 'A change to the development branch goes live with no human review first', which undercuts the email's promise that the answer goes in 'nas vossas palavras'.
The company page ends with no reply, correct or answer action; the only route to the three questions is the email reply.
The email is in Portuguese and the linked page is entirely in English, with no Portuguese line for the company it is addressed to.
Three names appear (PrompTugal.news, RiskMandate, web-summit.sgit.ai) and no legal entity or company behind the newsroom is named.
About names the source as 'SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__Web-Summit' while the footer on about-phone-s8 says 'github.com/PrompTugal/PrompTugal__News__Website'.
An editor is 'Vicky' on the front page and About but 'Vicky Wang' in bylines and footer, which makes a reader doubt she is a real person.
The graph shows Air Apps as 'United States' inside the 'Portuguese startups' cluster, which reads as an error and makes the founder distrust the map.
'(conferenceSlug lis26)' and 'newsroom@web-summit.dinis' as the re-checker are internal identifiers shown to a business reader.
'Who made this' lists agents, 'storyline S18' and 'desks/curator/README.md' but does not say plainly whether a person read the article.
The bold 'The independent newsroom' is qualified in the same paragraph by 'not independent of RiskMandate', which reads as overselling.
The 'What they do' description matches the company's own words, and the founder found nothing wrong to correct.
'independent of Web Summit, not of RiskMandate' stated plainly on the company page is the first thing that raises trust.
'Where this comes from' gives a real websummit.com URL and the date it was read, delivering on the email's 'cada facto tem a sua fonte e a data'.
'No one is listed under ChatPlace in the summit pages we have read' reassures the founder that her people were not dug up.
'A first-time founder could start at the first-timers meetup and go on to the data spaces masterclass' is useful advice with no pitch in it, and lifts the site in her eyes.
'The agent's own limits' answering Reach, Mandate, Gap for the newsroom itself makes the three questions feel fair rather than a sales script.
The email's 'Escrito por um agente de IA, revisto e enviado por mim' and the opt out line are read as more honest than typical media outreach.
